name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushAllState
signature: unsigned int* Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushAllState(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out)
summary: Flushes every pending PICA state group held by the command-buffer object: the fixed 9-slot block at +0x88, the 0x10-stride slot range at +0x1f8 and the 0x10-stride slot range at +0x3f8. It then appends a 20-word consecutive block (0x80000000 header, command word 0x000F0227, two count/index words and a 0x40-byte template copied from 0x0072F6A8) and returns the advanced output pointer.
evidence: No callers (called through function pointers); callees std_memcpy 0x00116C10 and FUN_00558210, the known PICA command-list writer. Literals 0x000F0227 and 0x0072F6A8 with a 0x40-byte memcpy. Cursors f_30 (9-slot block at +0x88), f_31/f_32 (slot range at +0x1f8, base command 0x20) and f_33/f_34 (slot range at +0x3f8, base command 0x40) are all reset after use; header uses the 0x80000000 consecutive-block flag.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushMatrixSlots
signature: void Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushMatrixSlots(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, unsigned char count)
summary: Emits the pending slice of the 32-slot, 0x10-byte-stride state array at self+0x1f8 (from cursor f_32 up to f_31, base command index cursor+0x20) into the PICA command list, then sets both the start and write cursors to count so the array can be refilled.
evidence: Callee FUN_00558210 (PICA command-list writer) and same caller pair as 0x0055851C/0x00558548 (FUN_00539A2C, FUN_0053AD18). Body: func_00558210(self,out, self+f_32*0x10+0x1f8, f_32+0x20, f_31-f_32) then f_31=arg3, f_32=arg3. Array stride 0x10 (= 4 words) and base offset 0x1f8 match the slot writes seen in FUN_0055877C (slots 0x20-0x24).

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushSlotBlock
signature: void Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushSlotBlock(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out)
summary: Emits the fixed 9-slot state block at self+0x88 (base command index 9, count f_30) into the command list and clears the dirty-slot count f_30.
evidence: Callee FUN_00558210; call func_00558210(self,arg2,&self->f_88,9,self->f_30) followed by f_30=0. Same 9-slot block that FUN_0055828C flushes first (also with base index 9), and the same caller pair FUN_00539A2C/FUN_0053AD18 as the neighbouring range flushers.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushUniformSlots
signature: void Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushUniformSlots(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, unsigned char count)
summary: Emits the pending slice of the 64-slot, 0x10-byte-stride state array at self+0x3f8 (cursor f_34 up to f_33, base command index cursor+0x40) into the command list and rewinds both cursors to count.
evidence: Callee FUN_00558210; call func_00558210(self,arg2, self+f_34*0x10+0x3f8, f_34+0x40, f_33-f_34) then f_33=arg3, f_34=arg3. Parallel structure to 0x005583F8 but on the second, larger array (+0x3f8, base 0x40) that 0x0055828C also flushes; callers FUN_00539A2C/FUN_0053AD18.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_SetMatrixBlock
signature: void Gfx_CmdBuf_SetMatrixBlock(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, const unsigned int* mtx)
summary: Copies a 16-word (4x4 float, 0x40-byte) matrix from the source descriptor into the transform block at self+0x38..+0x77 and emits the whole 5-slot block (base command index 0) to the command list, so the transform becomes active.
evidence: Body copies arg3[0..0xf] into f_38..f_74 (16 words = 0x40 bytes, exactly the block FUN_0055877C also fills from puVar2[0..0xf]) then calls func_00558210(self,arg2,&self->f_38,0,5) = 5 slots * 0x10 bytes = 0x50 bytes ending at +0x88. Caller FUN_0053CE64 (80b) is itself a PTRREF vtable slot; callee FUN_00558210.

name: maybe_Gfx_CopyBlock24
signature: void* maybe_Gfx_CopyBlock24(const void* src, void* dst)
summary: Copies a fixed 0x18-byte (24-byte, i.e. 6-word) record from src to dst and returns dst advanced past it; a small fixed-size record writer used when serialising state blocks into an output buffer.
evidence: Only callee is std_memcpy (0x00116C10) with size 0x18, return value is arg2+0x18. No callers and no literal references in the dossier, so the record type is unknown; the placement immediately after the command-buffer block writers (0x0055828C-0x00558584) and the identical structure of 0x00558698 (0x30 bytes) suggest fixed-size record copy helpers.

name: maybe_Gfx_CopyBlock48
signature: void* maybe_Gfx_CopyBlock48(const void* src, void* dst)
summary: Copies a fixed 0x30-byte (48-byte, 12-word) record from src to dst and returns dst advanced past it; the 0x30 size matches the state templates copied from 0x0072F608/0x0072F638 elsewhere in this region.
evidence: Only callee is std_memcpy with size 0x30, returns arg2+0x30. No callers/REFs in the dossier. 0x30-byte blocks are used by 0x0055877C (template g_0072F608) and 0x00558DC0 (template g_0072F638), implying this is the generic copy helper for such 48-byte state records.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_BuildRampParams
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_BuildRampParams(unsigned int* out, unsigned int unused, unsigned int start, unsigned int end)
summary: Builds a 3-word interpolation descriptor from two packed 8.24 fixed-point endpoints: it compares the 8-bit integer parts, clamps the extreme endpoint, computes 0xFF00/(delta+1) as a quantised step (right-shifted by 2, 3 or 4 and saturating at 0x1FE0), rewrites the start value's integer part and stores (start, end, shift-code | 0x40 when increasing).
evidence: Caller FUN_00539AC4 (same builder that calls the state-template writer 0x00558DC0). Body masks 0xff000000 from both inputs, replaces the exponent/integer byte with 0x08000000 or 0xf7000000 clamps, calls FUN_0011CFAC(0xff00, (delta>>24)+1) (division helper) against literal 0x00001FE0, and writes out[0]=start, out[1]=end, out[2]=shift(2/3/4)|0x40. Literal 0x00001FE0 is the only REF; the exact consumer of this ramp descriptor is unclear, hence maybe_.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitMaterialDraw
signature: unsigned int* Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitMaterialDraw(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, int* desc)
summary: Emits the complete PICA command sequence for drawing one material/pass pair: the 0x30-byte pipeline template (0x0072F548/0x0072F608), the 5-slot transform block, the 3+2 texture-matrix uniform slots at +0x1f8 (scale/offset/rotation derived from the instance fields f_28..f_34 and the short fields f_3c/f_3e), the shader/state blobs (desc->f_c with size f_14, or via 0x005575D0) and then repeats the stage for the second texture unit, returning the advanced output pointer.
evidence: PTRREF slot +0 in two tables (0x00781424 and 0x00781DA0, neighbours 0x005580AC, 0x00558E7C, 0x0053CE64, 0x0053CE08) i.e. a virtual 'emit' method. Literals 0x000200E0, 0x000F02B0, 0x7FFF0005, 0x000F00DB, 0x00200080, 0x7FFF0001, 0x7FFF0000, 0x000F02D6-adjacent templates 0x0072F548/0x0072F608 and float 0x3F800000/0x7FFF0005 flags; writes slots f_228..f_244 (slots 3-4 of the 0x1f8 array) after computing a texture matrix from f_28/f_2c/f_30/f_34 and sign-extended shorts f_3c/f_3e; callees FUN_00558210, FUN_005574F8, FUN_005575D0, FUN_00559B24, FUN_00559C54, std_memcpy.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteStateTemplate
signature: void Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteStateTemplate(unsigned int unused, unsigned int* out, unsigned int mode)
summary: Writes a 48-byte render-state template into the output block by copying the 0x30-byte constant template at 0x0072F638, then patches it for the requested mode (mode 2 clears word 5, mode 2 and 3 set word 6 to 0x0EEF0DFE and word 9 to 0x00010004) and, when bit 0x40 is set, replaces word 0 with 0x0EDE0EEE.
evidence: Caller FUN_00539AC4 (1716-byte draw-state builder, also caller of 0x005586BC). std_memcpy of 0x30 bytes from g_00558e30 (0x0072F638); REFs 0x0EEF0DFE, 0x00010004 and 0x0EDE0EEE; mode test (arg3 & 0xffffffbf) == 2 / == 3 and flag test (arg3 & 0x40). Param 1 is unused in the body.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlock
signature: int Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlock(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, unsigned int flags)
summary: Finishes a state block: if the pending counter f_30 is set it first flushes through 0x0053AD18, then clears the dirty counters (f_31..f_35) and, unless bit 0 is set in flags, copies the object's stored data block (pointer self->f_18, size f_1c) to the output and returns the 4-byte-aligned end pointer.
evidence: Callees std_memcpy and FUN_0053AD18 (the flush routine that in turn is a caller of 0x005583F8/0x0055851C/0x00558548). Body: if (self->f_30) out = FUN_0053AD18(); then f_35=f_31=f_32=f_33=f_34=0; if ((arg3&1)==0) memcpy(out,self->f_18,self->f_1c), out = (f_1c & ~3) + out. Field offsets match 0x00558E84, which is the same tail with the pending-state flush removed.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlockData
signature: int maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlockData(unsigned int* out, unsigned int unused, unsigned int flags, GfxCmdBuf* self)
summary: Same tail as 0x00558E4C but without the 0x0053AD18 pending-state flush: it clears the dirty counters of the command-buffer object (passed as the 4th argument) and, unless bit 0 of flags is set, copies the stored data block (f_18, f_1c bytes) to the output, returning the aligned end pointer.
evidence: No callers/REFs. Identical instruction sequence to 0x00558E4C (f_35=f_31=f_32=f_33=f_34=0; memcpy(out, f_18, f_1c); out=(f_1c&~3)+out) but the object arrives in arg4 instead of arg1 and there is no f_30 check or FUN_0053AD18 call, so the register/argument layout differs; exact call-site convention is unclear (hence maybe_).

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitStateBlob
signature: unsigned int* maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitStateBlob(GfxCmdBuf* self, unsigned int* out, unsigned int flags)
summary: When bit 0 of flags is clear, writes an 8-word state header (zeros with command words 0x0002006F and 0x00200080, a 0x1000 field and a 0x00200080-0x150000 offset) and then copies the object's inline blob (pointer at self+8, size self->f_c) into the command stream; finally marks the shader/state flags f_35/f_36 as set and clears the four bytes at +0x5f8.
evidence: Caller FUN_0053CE08 (92b), itself a PTRREF vtable slot; PTRREF at 0x00781D98 has 0x00558EE8 at +0 next to 0x00558E7C (+4), 0x0055877C (+8) and 0x005580AC (+12), i.e. a sibling 'emit' method of the same state class. REFs 0x0002006F and 0x00200080 used as PICA command words; inline memcpy of self->f_c bytes from *(u32*)(self+8); f_35=1, f_36=1, f_5f8..f_5fb=0. What the blob encodes (texture data vs shader code) is not determinable, hence maybe_.

name: Font_SetupTexture
signature: void Font_SetupTexture(FontRes* self)
summary: Re-initialises the font's embedded texture descriptor from the loaded resource: it takes the sub-resource at self[3]+0xc, queries a value through the object's vtable slot +0x7c, and passes the data address, format, width, height, size and flag into the texture-descriptor initialiser 0x0055A2BC.
evidence: Caller Font_LoadBffnt (0x00559D94) - authoritative name. Body: iVar2 = *(int*)(arg1[3]+0xc); uVar1 = (**(code**)(*arg1 + 0x7c))(); func_0055A2BC(arg1+4, 0, iVar2->f_14, *(u16*)(iVar2+10), iVar2->f_10, iVar2->f_12, uVar1, *(u32*)(iVar2+4), 1). Same vtable/dtor family as the Font object created by 0x00559144 (vtable 0x00781DB4).

name: Font_Create
signature: Font* Font_Create(void)
summary: Allocates a font object via 0x00559D4C, installs the base vtable 0x00781DB4, zeroes the resource pointers, initialises the embedded texture descriptor to the default (format 8) and stores the constant 0x00002206 in field 9; a conditional block afterwards re-derives the descriptor if a resource were already attached.
evidence: Caller FUN_0055A274 (which then overwrites the vtable) and called from Font_LoadResource; callees 0x00559D4C (object allocator, adjacent to Font_LoadBffnt 0x00559D94) and 0x0055A2BC (texture-descriptor init: func_0055A2BC(result+4,0,0,8,0,0,0,0,1)). PTRREF at 0x00781DB8 shows the vtable installed at 0x00781DB4 with RTTI pointers (0x00663874 typeinfo, 0x0066388C base) - a C++ class vtable. Literal 0x00002206 stored in result[9].

name: Font_DestructBase
signature: Font* Font_DestructBase(Font* self)
summary: Base-class destructor body: installs the base vtable 0x00781DB4 and resets the embedded texture descriptor to its empty default (format 8, no data), returning the object.
evidence: No callers listed (reached through function pointer / inlined into the derived destructor). Body: *arg1 = g_00559270 (0x00781DB4); func_0055A2BC(arg1+4,0,0,8,0,0,0,0,1). PTRREF at 0x00781DB8 (-4:0, +0:00559220, +8:0x00663874, +12:0x0066388C) confirms the vtable/RTTI pair of this class and that this function is the vtable's destructor slot.

name: maybe_Container_InitPairArray
signature: void maybe_Container_InitPairArray(unsigned int* self, unsigned int owner, unsigned int value)
summary: Initialises a small descriptor object: stores the two arguments (at +0 and +0xc), zeroes the other header words, then constructs an inline two-element array at +0x18 through std_ConstructArray with element size 4 and constructor 0x0051CF40.
evidence: Callers FUN_00557368 (100b) and FUN_005573E4 (44b) in the 0x00557xxx Gfx helper region (near the matrix/blob emitters 0x005574F8/0x005575D0). Callee std_ConstructArray (0x00100050) with literal ctor 0x0051CF40 and (4,2). Body only sets arg1[0]=arg2, arg1[1]=arg1[2]=arg1[4]=arg1[5]=0, arg1[3]=arg3; the owning class is not identifiable from the dossier (hence maybe_).

name: maybe_Font_EnsureDisplayList
signature: void maybe_Font_EnsureDisplayList(void* self)
summary: Lazy one-shot initialiser: if the built-flag at object+0x28 is clear it runs the 2412-byte display-list builder 0x005593E4 and then sets +0x28 = 1 and +0x29 = 0, so the static glyph command list is generated only once.
evidence: Body: if (self->f_28 == 0) { func_005593E4(self); self->f_28 = 1; self->f_29 = 0; }. Caller FUN_00536568 (80b). The guarded builder 0x005593E4 produces a static PICA command list and sits directly after the Font ctor/dtor cluster (0x00559144/0x00559220/0x0055935C), which is why Font is assumed; no literal evidence ties it to fonts (hence maybe_).

name: maybe_Font_BuildDisplayList
signature: void maybe_Font_BuildDisplayList(int* self, unsigned int base, unsigned int res)
summary: Builds a complete static GPU command list into the supplied buffer: it computes the total size from the resource's glyph/index counts, initialises two sub-streams (0x0051CFC4), fills a 0x8a0-byte ramp table (35 rows x 6 vec4 built from the table at 0x0072F8C0 and memset via 0x0051BD78), converts it with Os_VirtualToPhysical, emits the glyph quad commands (command words 0x0F02CC and 0x000F02D6), appends the per-character width/flag table and finishes by copying the constant templates 0x0072F930/0x0072F8D8/0x0072F570/0x0072F608/0x0072F668/0x0072F680.
evidence: Called only from 0x005593B4. Callees: Os_VirtualToPhysical (used on the 35-row ramp table), 0x0051CFC4/0x0051CF98/0x0051CFF0 (byte-stream init/append/align into a base address), 0x0051BD78, and std_ConstructArray; REFs 0x0072F8C0, 0x0072F6E8, 0x0072F530, 0x000F02D6, 0x0072F930, 0x0072F8D8, 0x1F1F1F1F, 0x0072F538, 0x00010700, 0x0072F570, 0x0072F608, 0x0072F668, 0x0072F680 plus the inline command word 0xf02cc, 0x140-byte and 0x94/0x98/0x30/0x18/0x28-byte template copies. The glyph table (u16 code/index/flags records, 7 char classes, 4 corner-colour flags) and the ramp table point at the text renderer, but the exact ownership (Font vs a generic UI renderer) is not proven, hence maybe_.

name: Font_CreateDerived
signature: void Font_CreateDerived(void)
summary: Creates the derived (resource-backed) font object: it calls the base constructor 0x00559144 and then overwrites the returned object's vtable with 0x00781F18, selecting the derived implementation; used by Font_LoadResource.
evidence: Caller Font_LoadResource (0x0053668C) - authoritative. Callee 0x00559144 (Font_Create); PTRREF at 0x0021FBC0 lists 0x0055A274 (+0) and REF literal 0x00781F18; body is just puVar1 = func_00559144(); *puVar1 = g_0055a288 (0x00781F18). The returned pointer is discarded, so the vtable assignment must target an object already registered inside 0x00559144.

name: Font_DestructDerived
signature: Font* Font_DestructDerived(Font* self)
summary: Derived-class destructor: restores the derived vtable 0x00781F18, releases the attached resource through 0x00559118 when self[2] is set, then chains to the base vtable 0x00781DB4 and resets the embedded texture descriptor to empty.
evidence: Body: *arg1 = g_0055a2b8 (0x00781F18); if (arg1[2]) func_00559118(arg1); *arg1 = g_00559270 (0x00781DB4); func_0055A2BC(arg1+4,0,0,8,0,0,0,0,1). PTRREF at 0x00781F1C (-4:0, +0:0055A28C, +8:0x00663874, +12:0x0066388C) - vtable/RTTI pair; the two vtable literals match Font_Create (0x00781DB4) and Font_CreateDerived (0x00781F18), and the trailing texturing reset matches Font_DestructBase.

name: Gfx_Texture_InitDesc
signature: void Gfx_Texture_InitDesc(unsigned int* desc, unsigned int cpuAddr, unsigned int vaddr, unsigned char format, unsigned short width, unsigned short height, unsigned short param7, unsigned int size, unsigned char flag)
summary: Fills a 0x14-byte texture/image descriptor: CPU pointer at +0, physical address (vaddr >> 3 after Os_VirtualToPhysical) at +4, width/height at +8/+0xa, a third u16 at +0xc, format byte at +0xe, flag byte at +0xf and size >> 3 at +0x10; vaddr 0 means 'no physical address'.
evidence: Called by 0x00558FF4, 0x00559144, 0x00559220 and 0x0055A28C. Only callee is Os_VirtualToPhysical (0x0012345C); body writes *desc=cpuAddr, desc[1]=phys>>3 (when vaddr!=0), *(u8*)(desc+0xe)=format, desc[4]=size>>3, *(u16*)(desc+0xa)=width, *(u16*)(desc+2)=height, *(u16*)(desc+3)=param7, *(u8*)(desc+0xf)=flag. Default call in the Font ctors is (0,0,8,0,0,0,0,1) = empty descriptor with format 8.

name: Gfx_ParseChipFile
signature: unsigned int Gfx_ParseChipFile(GfxChipFile* self, const void* data, unsigned int heap)
summary: Parses a 'CHIP' 2D-background container (RomFS '2d/bg/<map>/<map>.chp', 485 files): checks the magic/version template, reads the section count at +0xC and the section-table offset at +0xE, resolves the seven named sections (Header, Areas, AnimRGBA, AnimData, CharacterDepth, Name, BlockData00), stores their pointers in self (+0xC..+0x24), derives the pixel/aspect ratios with 0x0055A2BC and Mem_AllocAligned-allocates one 0x14-byte record per entry.
evidence: Format confirmed against the shipped assets, not just the code: 485 files named game_data/packs/2d/bg/<map>/<map>.chp start with the same header - 'CHIP' (0x50494843) +0, fileSize +4 (b001_101a.chp: 0x19210 = 102,928 = exact file length), BOM 0xFEFF + version 0x0102 +8 (the same bytes the parser compares against, stored literally at 0x00564B38: 'CHIP\0\0\0\0' 02 01 00 00), u16 section count 7 at +0xC, u16 section-table offset 0x18 at +0xE, then seven absolute section offsets at +0x18 (0x6C, 0xE8, 0x170, 0x1A8, 0x210, 0x23C, 0x29C). Each section is a 0x28-byte header {u16 headerSize=0x28, u16 flags, u32 payloadSize, char name[0x20]} followed by its payload, e.g. 'Header' at 0x6C (payload 0x54), 'Areas' at 0xE8 (0x60), 'AnimRGBA' 0x170, 'AnimData' 0x1A8, 'CharacterDepth' 0x210 (flags 3), 'Name' 0x23C (flags 1), 'BlockData00' 0x29C (0x18F4C bytes) - which matches the chain walk cur + u16@0 + u32@4 + u16@2 used in the body. Caller 0x002BD558 passes the loaded RomFS file plus a per-resource offset. Return 1 on success, 0 on bad magic/version.

name: Gfx_Material_ResolveTextures
signature: void Gfx_Material_ResolveTextures(GfxMaterial* self)
summary: Resolves the material's texture indices into real texture objects: after resetting the sub-object at self+8, it looks up the three u8 indices at desc+0x1f..0x21 in the descriptor's pointer table and binds them at self+0x58/+0x5c/+0x60, plus the base/animated texture indices into self+0x1c/+0x40/+0x4c according to the mode byte at self+0x64 (0, 1 or 2 textures).
evidence: Callers FUN_0049D84C, FUN_004E2A70, FUN_005A8000 (shared scene/battle/UI draw paths). Callees FUN_005644E0 (arg1+8 reset), FUN_00712BBC (388b) and FUN_00712FEC/FUN_0071312C - three setters taking a resolved resource pointer plus a destination field; index table is *(u32*)(*(int*)(*(int*)(arg1+4)+0xc) + idx*4) with 0xff meaning 'none'; destinations 0x1c, 0x40, 0x4c, 0x58, 0x5c, 0x60 and mode switch on the byte at arg1+100 (0x64).

name: maybe_Container_InitListObject
signature: void maybe_Container_InitListObject(unsigned int* self, unsigned int owner)
summary: Constructor of a small list/array container: installs vtable 0x00782080, initialises a self-referential two-node link structure (+4/+0x10 point back to self, +0x14/+0x18 to self+4), stores owner twice at +8/+0xc, zeroes six u16 counters at +0x1c..+0x27 and constructs the inline 4-byte-element array at +0x28.
evidence: No callers/REFs besides the vtable literal g_0055acf8 = 0x00782080 and the array constructor literal g_0055acfc = 0x00146A44 passed to std_ConstructArray(arg1+10, 0x00146A44, 4). Written fields: arg1[1]=arg1, arg1[4]=arg1, arg1[5]=arg1+4, arg1[6]=arg1+4, arg1[2]=arg1[3]=arg2, u16 zeros at 0x1c,0x1e,0x20,0x22,0x24,0x26; the element type and owner class cannot be determined (hence maybe_).

name: Gfx_Overlay_AddQuad
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_AddQuad(GfxOverlay* self, const void* quad, int scale)
summary: Appends one screen-space quad to the global 2D batch: after a one-time init of the singleton at 0x008384A0 (memset 0x140, vtable 0x00782AFC), it converts the descriptor's pixel rect and UVs into normalised coordinates using the screen mode (320x240 for mode 2, 400x480 otherwise), picks a palette colour when the descriptor's colour index is >= 0, and writes the 0x48-byte (18-word) vertex record (pos, size, uv, 8 colour words, 3 table colours, flag) at buffer[count*0x48], incrementing the count.
evidence: Callers FUN_002D3C1C (maybe_Gfx_Overlay_DrawFourQuads) and FUN_002D4604 - the 2D overlay drawing paths, same pair that calls 0x0055CB58/0x0055CCB4. Body: singleton flag *g_007BE38C, buffer base from literal 0x008384A0, memset 0x140 via FUN_00116AE0, vtable 0x00782AFC, std_ConstructArray(puVar5+10, 0x0051CF40, 4); screen-size selection self->f_24==2 -> 0x140/0xf0 else 400/0x1e0; UV/rect fields read from arg2->f_1c..f_30, colours from f_32..f_3b and palette index f_3c (table entry bytes +0x74/0x75/0x76 scaled by 0x3B808081), current colour from g_007E2030, target record stride 0x48 with the write cursor piVar6[2].

name: Gfx_CharShadowPass_Create
signature: unsigned int Gfx_CharShadowPass_Create(GfxCharShadowPass* self, unsigned int ctx, unsigned int heap)
summary: Allocates the character-shadow-pass resources: it builds five resource descriptors (slots 0-5 with sizes 0xec0/0xc00 and formats 3/1) and registers them through 0x0055F8B8 on the current command list, then allocates a 0x1800-byte block (128 objects of 0x30 bytes) with Mem_AllocAligned and constructs it with 0x0055B980, clearing the cursor at self[7].
evidence: Caller Gfx_CharShadowPass_Init (0x002D4F28) - authoritative name. Callees maybe_Gfx_CmdList_GetSingleton (0x006F2394), maybe_Gfx_ResourceTable_InsertRange (0x0055F8B8), Mem_AllocAligned (size 0x1800, align 4) and std_ConstructArray with ctor 0x0055B980, element size 0x30, count 0x80 (0x80*0x30 = 0x1800). Stack descriptors: {0,1,0xec0,3}, {2,-1,0xc00,1}, {3,-1,0xc00,1}, {4,-1,0xc00,1}, {5,-1,0xc00,1}; REF literal 0x0055B980; returns 1.

name: Gfx_CmdList_BindTexture
